Bring consistency and empathy to return review without automating the decision.

Summarizes anonymous synthetic return evidence, classifies complaint themes, drafts policy-grounded options, and surfaces aggregate quality trends.

**Why try it:** It helps service, quality, and loss-prevention teams review the same evidence while preserving authorization, privacy, and non-accusatory language.

## Problem Statement

Return and complaint workflows can become inconsistent, slow, and difficult to learn from when policy evidence, product signals, and service context are fragmented.

## Solution Summary

The agent converts CRM- and ERP-style synthetic case records into structured decision support for human review in Microsoft collaboration workflows.

**Blueprint role:** Human-approved service decision support

**Capabilities:** Anonymous return review; Privacy-safe complaint classification; Human-approved resolution options; Aggregate returns and quality trends. See [responsibilities and trust boundaries](2.Architecture.md).

## Business Outcomes

- More consistent review summaries

Claims are qualitative; synthetic demo figures are not customer results or performance commitments. See the [claims policy](../../solutions/README.md#claims-policy).

## Target Users

| Role | Need |
| --- | --- |
| Customer Service Agents | Review anonymous return evidence, classify concerns and draft policy-grounded options, with every action kept behind authorization. |
| Quality Teams | Review aggregate defect and return patterns without accusing any person. |
| Loss Prevention Teams | Review policy exceptions and suspicious aggregate patterns in non-accusatory language. |

## In Scope / Out of Scope

### In scope

- Summarize anonymous return evidence (case label, product, reason, condition, days, channel and review state) and name missing review evidence.
- Classify a complaint with category, rationale and severity context, without echoing personal or sensitive text.
- Compare reason, condition, window and impacts against packaged playbooks and present an option for authorized review.
- Summarize monthly return rates, reasons, resolution time, satisfaction and quality signals, separating quality review from suspicious-pattern review.

### Out of scope / approval boundary

- No return, refund, credit, replacement, shipment, reservation, account change or customer message is approved, processed or sent.
- No repetition of personal or sensitive free text from a complaint.
- No accusation of fraud or misconduct against a person; suspicious patterns stay aggregate.
- No live CRM, order or policy lookups; only the uploaded anonymous synthetic cases, trends and rules are used.
- No fabricated or approximated identifiers; an unknown ID stops the answer.
- No workshop publishing: validated agents stay in Draft and publication requires explicit confirmation.

## Qualification Checklist

- [ ] Is a Microsoft Copilot Studio target environment, with an approved publisher prefix, available for the returns build?
- [ ] Can the delivery team authenticate with PAC CLI 2.9.3 or newer and initialize a `cli-copilot` project, or follow the manual upload path?
- [ ] Has the customer mapped case and order evidence to Dynamics 365 CRM and ERP and policy content to SharePoint governed policy knowledge?
- [ ] Will every production connection start read-only, with all write actions kept separate?
- [ ] Does the authorized resolution workflow provide authenticated tools, authorization checks, explicit human approval and an audit log?
- [ ] Are service, quality and loss-prevention reviewers named, with privacy and non-accusation rules agreed?
- [ ] Is publication held for explicit confirmation after replaying RCR-01 through RCR-04 against the reviewed instructions, knowledge, skills and model?
- [ ] Have governance, telemetry, support and success measures been agreed for production returns and complaints handling?

## What Actually Goes Wrong

- **option-read-as-approval:** A draft resolution option is read as an approved refund, credit or exchange.
- **personal-text-echoed:** Names, contacts, account details or payment data from complaint text appear in the answer.
- **individual-accused:** An aggregate pattern becomes an accusation of fraud against a person.
- **unknown-identifier-approximated:** An unknown return ID is answered with a similar case.
- **production-data-mismatch:** Production data differs from the synthetic records the skills were tested on.
- **missing-grounding:** A skill or its knowledge cannot load, but the agent answers from memory.

See [state and recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery).
